subject: OpenAPI client toggle + streaming drop triage (ClearHelix POC)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@clearhelix.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@clearhelix.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming drops during POC + ask about OpenAPI client toggle

Hi Logan / Marissa,

During our ClearHelix POC today we hit repeated streaming disconnections when a single large prompt (~14k tokens) is sent. The UI receives a final "connection closed" at ~60s and the SDK client attempts an auto-reconnect which causes duplicate partial outputs. I've attached the client trace (clearhelix_stream_trace.txt) and a screenshot of the UI failure.

Two quick asks:
- Is there a runtime-side toggle we can set (OpenAPI param or header) to force synchronous/non-streaming responses per-request so we can avoid client reconnect logic while we triage?
- If not, can your runtime team triage whether this is a connection lease/keepalive/stream fragmentation issue?

This is blocking our demo next week — can we escalate to engineering? We're happy to provide a repro script; attaching a minimal cURL/SDK repro.

Thanks,
Samir
CTO, ClearHelix

Attachments: clearhelix_stream_trace.txt, screenshot_streaming_trace.png, repro_script.sh

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearhelix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming drops during POC + ask about OpenAPI client toggle

Samir — thanks for the repro and traces, and sorry you're hitting this during the POC. Looping in platform/runtime (Karthik) and field eng (Soojin) to triage.

High-level ask from ClearHelix: a per-request way to avoid streaming (or an explicit OpenAPI param/header) so their client doesn't attempt reconnects while we investigate. Secondary: full triage to identify if this is a keepalive/connection-lease or server-side stream fragmentation.

Proposed immediate plan:
1) Karthik/Soojin: confirm whether an escape hatch exists (OpenAPI param or SDK flag) that forces non-streaming (synchronous) responses. If there isn't one, recommend a short-term fallback (explicit route to non-stream endpoint or disable streaming in proxy). Goal: within 24 hours.
2) Field reproduction: Soojin will reproduce using the attached repro_script.sh and the clearhelix traces. Identify whether the server closes stream or client sees TCP reset.
3) If server-side, open SUP ticket and propose a canary patch or routing switch to prevent disconnects for the ClearHelix demo.

Samir: can you confirm which SDK version you're using (npm package or pip) and whether you were using the official OpenAPI JS client or an internal wrapper? Also, please grant redwood-drive access to the attached trace folder so engineering can fetch logs.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync for tomorrow morning (PST) to review findings and align a mitigation.

— Logan
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@clearhelix.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming drops during POC + ask about OpenAPI client toggle

Thanks for the context. Quick notes from runtime side after a first pass:

- There is no officially documented per-request "force-non-streaming" OpenAPI param today. Streaming vs non-streaming is negotiated by the client call pattern (event stream vs single-response call). We do have an internal header that can route to the non-streaming code path, but it's not exposed in the public SDK.

- The behaviour you describe (disconnect at ~60s with client auto-reconnects) suggests either a connection-lease/idle timeout at the LB layer or a streaming buffer flush bug when responses exceed our typical window. We need a repro that exercises a large token response and captures the server tcpdump / nginx proxy logs.

Immediate next steps I can own:
1) Create a short-lived feature flag/header that routes requests to the non-streaming path for a specific customer (internal header X-RW-Force-Blocking: 1). I'll spin up a canary route and coordinate with infra. Estimated: prototype today, canary tomorrow.
2) Opened JIRA SUP-4821 to track the triage. Will add logs and outcome.
3) Need the exact SDK version + reproduction steps (Samir, please confirm). If Samir used the JS official client, we can add a per-request option in the client within a small patch, but that needs product approval for an SDK release.

Temporary mitigation: Soojin — please run the repro with curl (no client recon) and the official node client so we can compare whether the reconnect is client-driven. If we see server close without a TCP FIN from the client, that's a runtime bug.

I'll be available on the sync Logan sets — will have a demo of the canary header if infra agrees.

— Karthik (Platform/Runtime)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearhelix.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming drops during POC + ask about OpenAPI client toggle

On Tue, Apr 3, 2028 at 11:14 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> There is no officially documented per-request "force-non-streaming" OpenAPI param today...

Thanks — I'll take the field reproduction. Samir: I started a shared drive folder and requested read access using the email you used on the POC. Please accept so I can pull the traces. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEF

What I'll run today:
- repro_script.sh (attached) against our canary routing and against raw curl to observe differences
- collect tcpdump/conntrack logs on the canary host if the stream closes
- compare client-side reconnect timing vs server FIN/RESET

Deliverables by EOD PST: summary (pass/fail), raw capture, and recommended short-term mitigation (canary header or routing switch). If we can confirm server closes, Karthik please be ready to accept the SUP ticket for engineering triage.

— Soojin (Sales Engineering / Field)

From: Samir Patel <samir@clearhelix.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@clearhelix.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming drops during POC + ask about OpenAPI client toggle

Thanks all — I accepted the Drive invite and gave read access to the folder. We've also confirmed the team is using the official OpenAPI JS client v2.4.1 and a lightweight internal wrapper.

If you can push a canary X-RW-Force-Blocking header for the ClearHelix routing, that would unblock the demo. We're good for the 30-min sync tomorrow morning PST. Please confirm the canary window (how long it will be active) and whether this header will be supported safely in production if we need to rely on it longer term.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Samir
CTO, ClearHelix
